page: The Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is a Cloud Compute virtual server featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor. It is configured with 6 shared vCPUs, derived from 3 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 320 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU acceleration is present on this instance type.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core processing is limited, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the weak and poor categories respectively. Multi-core performance is relatively stronger, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench ray tracing achieving average ratings. Memory read bandwidth is average at 407.68 GB/sec for cached small blocks, but large-block write bandwidth is weak at 18.72 GB/sec. Data compression and decompression tasks show poor performance, as evidenced by low single-threaded gzip and multi-threaded bzip3 throughput.

Due to the shared CPU allocation, this server exhibits resource contention risks, making it less suitable for CPU-intensive production workloads. However, it maintains average performance for Redis SET operations and small-model LLM text generation. The combination of a 320 GB NVMe SSD and 16.0 GB of RAM offers a cost-effective profile for budget-conscious deployments. It is best suited for general-purpose development environments, basic web serving, caching layers, and lightweight multi-threaded applications that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance.
